CHAIRPERSON’S MESSAGE
• Group earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 
(EBITDA) at Rs.16.35 billion in the first quarter of the financial year 
2026/27 increased by 26% over the EBITDA of Rs.12.97 billion recorded 
in 2025/26.
• The profit attributable to equity holders in the first quarter of the 
financial year 2026/27 was Rs.62 million, compared to a loss of Rs.804 
million in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. The 
profit attributable to equity holders for the first quarter of 2026/27 
excluding net exchange losses was Rs.1.95 billion [2025/26 Q1: loss of 
Rs.418 million]. 
• Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT), the project company 
of West Container Terminal (WCT-1) continued its strong ramp-
up, with throughput exceeding plan. The terminal has effectively 
reached full utilisation of its phase 1 capacity based on the recent 
run rate of volumes and demonstrates further growth potential. The 
development and operationalisation of the full terminal remains on 
track for December 2026.
• The profitability of the Transportation industry group was mainly 
driven by the Group's Bunkering business, Lanka Marine Services 
(LMS) and CWIT.
• Profitability of the Leisure industry group was impacted by the 
challenging operating environment as the conflict in the Middle East 
disrupted travel and weakened travel sentiment across several key 
source markets.
• City of Dreams Sri Lanka continued its positive momentum during 
the quarter. Growth in hotel EBITDA was driven by an increase in 
occupancy and ARRs. The casino continues to record a steadily 
improving performance, where the Group recognises rental income. 
• The Beverages and Confectionery businesses recorded strong volume 
growth of 27% and 13%, respectively which supported the growth in 
profitability. 
• JKH will diversify its Consumer Foods portfolio into Sri Lanka's 
Quick Service Restaurant (QSR) segment through the rollout of the 
internationally recognised ‘Wendy’s’ brand. The relevant franchise 
agreements and other preliminary work have already been concluded 
with the first outlet expected to open by December 2026.
• The Supermarket business recorded strong growth during the quarter, 
with same-store sales increasing by 13%, driven by average basket 
value (ABV) growth of 7% and customer footfall growth of 6%.  
• John Keells CG Auto (JKCG) continues to witness strong vehicle 
demand and volume growth, with over 2,400 vehicles handed over 
during the quarter, although profitability moderated due to a shift in 
sales mix, with a higher proportion of vehicle handovers stemming 
from the lower-priced segments.
• The Property industry group recorded an increase in EBITDA driven 
by profit recognition from sales of units at the VIMAN, TRI-ZEN and 
Cinnamon Life residential development projects. 
• NTB delivered a robust performance during the quarter, supported 
by healthy loan growth and the successful integration of the retail 
banking franchise of HSBC Sri Lanka, effective 1 May 2026. Union 
Assurance (UA) recorded encouraging double-digit growth in gross 
written premiums, primarily attributable to renewal business.
• The Group's carbon footprint per million Rupees of revenue decreased 
by 12.2% to 0.33 MT, while water withdrawal per million Rupees of 
revenue decreased by 8.4% to 4.62 cubic meters.

CHAIRPERSON’S MESSAGE
Sri Lanka witnessed continued macroeconomic stability during the 
period under review, with economic activity remaining resilient despite 
the uncertain and volatile global backdrop. Supported by continued 
gross domestic product (GDP) growth and improving domestic demand, 
the economy recorded broad-based progress across several sectors. The 
stability achieved under the country's economic recovery programme 
helped sustain business and consumer confidence, creating a favourable 
operating environment for the Group and supporting performance 
across a number of its businesses.
While the conflict in the Middle East contributed to higher energy 
costs, increased transportation expenses and disruptions to regional 
travel flows, the broader economic impact on Sri Lanka remained 
manageable. The external sector continued to be supported by resilient 
worker remittances, tourism earnings and expected multilateral inflows, 
while the conditions in the foreign currency market showed signs of 
stabilisation towards the latter part of the period. Gross official reserves 
stood at approximately USD 6.5 billion at end June 2026, reflecting 
scheduled foreign debt servicing and net foreign exchange sales by the 
Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL).
Inflation increased during the quarter, reaching 6.8% in June 2026, 
driven primarily by higher global energy prices and domestic utility 
tariff revisions. In response to rising inflationary pressures and elevated 
external risks, the CBSL increased its Overnight Policy Rate by 100 basis 
points to 8.75% on 26 May 2026, marking the first policy rate increase 
in over three years. The increase was aimed at anchoring inflation 
expectations, maintaining price stability and supporting the external 
sector. The Sri Lankan Rupee also witnessed pressure during the quarter, 
depreciating against the US Dollar amid heightened global uncertainty 
and geopolitical developments. While the currency stabilised towards 
the end of the quarter, the exchange rate as of 30 June 2026 was Rs.337 
to the US Dollar as against Rs.315 as of 31 March 2026. The depreciation 
of the Rupee helped businesses with foreign currency denominated 
revenue streams while it had an immediate translation impact on the 
net foreign currency exposure of the Group of approximately USD 100 
million.
The tourism sector experienced a setback during the quarter as 
geopolitical developments affected travel sentiment and disrupted 
connectivity through key transit hubs. As a result, tourist arrivals 
declined by 9% year-on-year to approximately 406,000 visitors during 
the period from April to June 2026. This period typically represents 
an off-peak season for Sri Lanka's tourism industry. Encouragingly, 
forward booking trends have strengthened in recent weeks despite 
the seasonal moderation in demand. While the operating environment 
remains impacted by the conflict in the Middle East, Sri Lanka remains 
well positioned to benefit from the continued growth in regional travel 
demand over the medium-term, particularly from India, one of the 
country's most important source markets.
Sri Lanka continued to make progress under the IMF-supported reform 
programme during the period, successfully completing the Fifth and 
Sixth Reviews under the Extended Fund Facility in May 2026. This 
resulted in disbursements of approximately USD 695 million, bringing 
cumulative disbursements under the programme to approximately USD 
2.4 billion. 
Overall, Sri Lanka enters the second half of 2026 with a stable 
macroeconomic environment, continued progress on structural reforms 
and improving economic fundamentals, providing confidence in the 
country's medium-term growth prospects notwithstanding the volatility 
on account of the Middle East conflict and related disruptions.
GROUP PERFORMANCE 
Group revenue at Rs.141.65 billion for the period under review increased 
by 24% over the Rs.114.15 billion recorded in the first quarter of the 
previous financial year. 
Group earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 
(EBITDA) at Rs.16.35 billion in the first quarter of the financial year 
2026/27 increased by 26% over the EBITDA of Rs.12.97 billion recorded 
in 2025/26.
Group profit before tax (PBT) at Rs.4.08 billion in the first quarter of the 
financial year 2026/27 increased by 31% over Rs.3.11 billion recorded in 
the previous financial year. Group PBT recorded an increase during the 
quarter despite a net exchange loss of Rs.1.89 billion [2025/26 Q1: loss of 
Rs.388 million], mainly arising due to the impact of the depreciation of 
the Rupee on the foreign currency denominated long-term loan at City 
of Dreams Sri Lanka, amounting to Rs.3.83 billion. Group PBT for the first 
quarter of 2026/27, excluding net exchange losses, increased to Rs.5.97 
billion [2025/26 Q1: Rs.3.49 billion].
Group profit after tax (PAT) at Rs.773 million in the first quarter of the 
financial year 2026/27 is an increase of 8% over the Rs.717 million 
recorded in the previous financial year. PAT was impacted by an increase 
in tax expenses arising from higher withholding tax on dividends 
received. The PAT for the first quarter of 2026/27 excluding net exchange 
losses was Rs.2.67 billion [2025/26 Q1: Rs.1.11 billion]. 
The profit attributable to equity holders in the first quarter of the 
financial year 2026/27 was Rs.62 million, compared to a loss of Rs.804 
million in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. The 
profit attributable to equity holders for the first quarter of 2026/27 
excluding net exchange losses was Rs.1.95 billion [2025/26 Q1: loss of 
Rs.418 million]. 
The Company PBT for the first quarter of 2026/27 at Rs.5.66 billion is an 
increase over Rs.1.52 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 
2025/26 due to the abovementioned higher dividend receipts.  
TRANSPORTATION
The Transportation industry group EBITDA of Rs.5.01 billion in the first 
quarter of 2026/27 represents significant growth of 223% over the 
EBITDA for the first quarter of the previous financial year [2025/26 
Q1: Rs.1.55 billion]. The increase in profitability was mainly due to the 
performance of the Group's Bunkering business, Lanka Marine Services 
(LMS) and Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT), the project 
company of West Container Terminal (WCT-1).
LMS recorded a substantial improvement in profitability, supported 
by a 38% increase in volumes and a growth in margins. Performance 
benefited from heightened demand arising from supply chain 
disruptions linked to the conflict in the Middle East while volatility in 
energy prices aided margins.
